findings.claim: getDataWithMetadata takes the length from the GET response's Content-Length, which under the default multipart client is part 1's size, not the object's.
findings.failure_mode: If merged as-is, any complex obs over 8 MiB stored in S3 by the multipart client reports length 8388608; legacyui's ComplexObsServlet sends getLength() as Content-Length, so downloads are silently cut at 8 MiB, where master's separate HEAD returned the full size.
findings.evidence: Read SDK 2.32.13 sources (bom awsSdkS3Version): DownloadObjectHelper.downloadObject splits into partNumber GETs (MultipartDownloaderSubscriber.nextRequest), SplittingTransformer forwards only the first onResponse upstream; DEFAULT_MIN_PART_SIZE=8 MiB. Ran a throwaway JUnit test driving the real S3StorageService against a local HttpServer emulating S3 partNumber responses (20 MiB object, 3 parts): multipart=true -> metadataLength=8388608, bytesRead=20971520; control multipart=false -> 20971520/20971520. With the suggested getObjectLength applied: 20971520 under multipart; spotless:apply left it unchanged. javap of legacyui-omod 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT ComplexObsServlet: ComplexData.getLength() -> setHeader("Content-Length"). Against S3Mock 4.5.0 (the IT's container): a 20 MiB object saved through S3StorageService answers a partNumber=1 GET with contentLength=20971520, contentRange=null, partsCount=null, so S3Mock ignores partNumber; S3StorageServiceIT runs 28 tests green at head and cannot see the bug.

findings.claim: read() falls back to the legacy location only on NoSuchFileException, but a legacy key whose encoded name exceeds 255 bytes fails the current-location stat with FileSystemException (File name too long), so the legacy file is never tried.
findings.failure_mode: If merged as-is, pre-2.8 complex obs whose titles have about 36+ two-byte (e.g. Cyrillic) characters stop loading after upgrade: AbstractHandler throws UncheckedIOException, TextHandler throws APIException, ImageHandler silently returns no image, where master read them from the legacy location.
findings.evidence: Pre-2.8 naming read at df94143ec (80b4411f8^) AbstractHandler.getOutputFileToWrite: title_uuid.ext in the obs dir. encodeKey (BaseStorageService:110-115) URL-encodes non-ASCII bytes. Throwaway test with storage/complex_obs present: head, 36 Cyrillic letters -> FileSystemException '...%2Etxt: File name too long'; controls 34 letters and ASCII read OK. Same test with master's LocalStorageService: all three read OK. With the suggested read() applied: all read OK, LocalStorageServiceTest (36) and the six handler test classes green; spotless:apply only drops the now-unused NoSuchFileException import. Without storage/complex_obs present the long name read OK (ENOENT on the parent wins), so a regression test must create that directory. Linux: in a python:3.12-alpine container (kernel 5.15) stat on the 259-byte encoded name returns ENAMETOOLONG (control: short missing name -> ENOENT); JDK 21 UnixException.translateToIOException maps only ENOENT to NoSuchFileException and everything else except EACCES/EEXIST to FileSystemException, so read() fails the same way on Linux.

findings.claim: The only call-count test exercises AbstractHandler.getObs, which all five bundled handlers override, so TRUNK-6682's acceptance criterion (tests preventing reintroduction of redundant calls) is unmet for the handlers that actually serve reads.
findings.failure_mode: If merged as-is, re-adding a redundant exists or getMetadata call to any bundled handler passes CI, so the per-read savings this PR delivers can regress unnoticed, contrary to the ticket's explicit acceptance criterion.
findings.evidence: grep: getObs(Obs obs, String view) is overridden in BinaryDataHandler, BinaryStreamHandler, ImageHandler, MediaHandler, TextHandler. Mutation: added storageService.exists(key) in BinaryStreamHandler, getMetadata in TextHandler, 2-arg injectMissingMetadata in MediaHandler -> AbstractHandlerTest + 5 handler test classes: 32 tests green. Control: same 2-arg injectMissingMetadata in AbstractHandler.getObs -> getObs_shouldNotIssueRedundantStorageCallsForLocalStorage fails (expected 0, was 1). A throwaway TextHandler test using ReflectionTestUtils.setField(handler, "storageService", countingDelegate) passed at head and failed with the TextHandler mutation.

findings.claim: exists() no longer checks that the current-location path stays inside the storage dir, so an absolute key reports whether any file on the host exists instead of being refused.
findings.evidence: Throwaway test at head: exists("/etc/passwd")=true, exists("/etc/nonexistent-wt05")=false, getData("/etc/passwd") throws IllegalArgumentException. Same test with master's LocalStorageService: both exists calls throw IllegalArgumentException. encodeKey keeps '/', so storageDir.resolve("/etc/passwd") is absolute. With the suggested line applied: exists("/etc/passwd") throws IAE again, LocalStorageServiceTest green, spotless leaves it unchanged.

findings.claim: The obs-dir null guard and its test fix a pre-existing master NPE unrelated to TRUNK-6682's I/O counts.
findings.evidence: Swapped in master's ImageHandler and ran ImageHandlerTest: getObs_shouldNotThrowWhenTheObsDirGlobalPropertyHasNoValue errors with NullPointerException ('this.pattern' is null) from key.replaceFirst(getObsDir(), ""). The guard arrived in 07338baf4 with no review thread asking for it.
findings.body: Could this guard and `getObs_shouldNotThrowWhenTheObsDirGlobalPropertyHasNoValue` go in their own ticket? Master throws the same NPE here for a bare-extension title whenever the obs dir property is unset, so it's a separate fix from the I/O counts, and keeping it out leaves less to verify here. Nothing breaks with it in.

findings.claim: S3StorageService.getData duplicates getDataWithMetadata's GetObject call and 404 translation.
findings.evidence: Read S3StorageService:129-156 at head. Applied the delegation together with the other fixes; spotless:apply left it unchanged and the api tests listed above compiled and passed (S3 IT not run).
findings.body:
This can just delegate to `getDataWithMetadata`, which repeats the same GetObject call and 404 translation (the kind of duplication ibacher flagged in `LocalStorageService`, [comment](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-core/pull/6535#discussion_r3990739410)), since the GET already carries the headers:

```suggestion
		return getDataWithMetadata(key).data();
```

findings.claim: Reply in the existing thread (comment 4070873940): new-layout reads now take one existence check, but legacy-layout obs still take three Files.exists calls plus a failed stat, so the ticket's 'at most one existence-related check' holds only for obs saved after 2.8.
findings.evidence: Throwaway test with a counting LocalStorageService subclass replaying parseDataKey + getDataWithMetadata: legacy obs under complex_obs/ -> fileExists=3; new-layout key -> fileExists=1. The failed stat is read()'s first reader.apply on the current location (LocalStorageService:93-100). Thread 4070873940 asked whether the ticket stays open for layout resolution and has no reply.
findings.body: New-layout reads are down to one `Files.exists` now, but a legacy-layout obs (everything saved before 2.8) still takes three plus a failed stat before the read. Does TRUNK-6682 stay open for those, or should the description say its three-operation figure covers new-layout obs only?

verdict: Not ready to merge: on S3 with the default multipart client, getDataWithMetadata reports part 1's size as the object's length, so complex obs over 8 MiB are silently served truncated.
